s1.syndrome_frame: chronic swelling and discomfort in the oral cavity with fluctuating pain intensity and sensation of heaviness
salient_findings: slowly growing swelling in the right upper vestibule
firm, mildly tender diffuse swelling of the adjacent vestibular mucosa
mild periapical radiolucency at the affected root apices
key_facts: 45-year-old woman
2-month history of symptoms
swelling and discomfort in the right upper vestibule
fluctuations in pain intensity
sensation of heaviness in the area
teeth #15 and #16 are grossly carious
no tenderness on percussion of the involved teeth
mild periapical radiolucency on panoramic radiography
preoperative blood tests are within normal limits
gelatinous, soft, mushy tissue obtained on curettage

shortlist.label: Periapical granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: matches the clinical presentation of a swelling with fluctuating pain intensity and the histopathological finding of a gelatinous, soft, mushy tissue

shortlist.label: Periapical cyst
shortlist.why_kept: consistent with the panoramic radiography finding of a mild periapical radiolucency and the clinical presentation of a chronic swelling

shortlist.label: Periapical abscess
shortlist.why_kept: considered due to the presence of a swelling and discomfort in the right upper vestibule, although the absence of tenderness on percussion makes it less likely

shortlist.label: Radicular cyst
shortlist.why_kept: a possible diagnosis given the presence of a carious tooth and a periapical radiolucency, although the clinical presentation is more suggestive of a granuloma

shortlist.label: Chronic sclerosing osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: a rare but possible diagnosis that could explain the chronic swelling and discomfort, although the lack of systemic symptoms and the presence of a carious tooth make it less likely

raw.rationale: The presence of a gelatinous, soft, mushy tissue on curettage and the lack of acute symptoms such as severe pain or swelling suggest a chronic inflammatory process, which is more consistent with a periapical granuloma than an abscess. The mild periapical radiolucency also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Periapical abscess
rejected.why: Lack of acute symptoms and presence of gelatinous tissue on curettage

rejected.label: Periapical cyst
rejected.why: Curettage yielded soft tissue, not a cystic structure

rejected.label: Radicular cyst
rejected.why: Clinical presentation and histopathological findings do not support a cystic lesion

rejected.label: Chronic sclerosing osteomyelitis
rejected.why: Radiographic findings do not show sclerotic changes typical of osteomyelitis
